papers.title: FlowBatt: Flow Matching for Probabilistic Battery Degradation Prediction
papers.abstract: Battery degradation remains a central challenge in the development and broad application of sustainable energy technologies. Accurate degradation prediction is challenging, as battery aging emerges from complex and heterogeneous interactions among cycling behavior, operating conditions, and cell chemistry. Existing machine-learning approaches typically focus on deterministic end-of-life predictions or modeling degradation curves within fixed chemistry settings, leaving probabilistic state of health (SOH) trajectory modeling across heterogeneous chemistries underexplored. We introduce FlowBatt, a use-inspired conditional generative framework that adapts flow matching with a diffusion transformer (DiT) backbone to battery degradation trajectory modeling. FlowBatt models full SOH trajectories as probabilistic degradation processes conditioned on early-cycle capacity data. To strengthen this conditioning pathway, we use explainable AI analysis to diagnose and improve the encoder that maps early-cycle capacity matrices into conditioning vectors. We evaluate FlowBatt on five public benchmark settings spanning diverse chemistries and aging conditions, comparing it with supervised and diffusion-based trajectory models as well as established baselines for remaining useful life (RUL) prediction under shared data splits. FlowBatt achieves the best trajectory-wise SOH prediction performance on all five datasets, with errors below 2.5%, and delivers competitive RUL prediction performance. By generating multiple plausible trajectories, FlowBatt provides empirical prediction intervals for battery degradation modeling. These results indicate that flow-matching-based trajectory modeling is a promising framework for probabilistic battery health prediction.

insight.tldr: FlowBatt is a conditional generative framework adapting flow matching with a diffusion transformer backbone to model probabilistic battery degradation trajectories.
insight.problem: Battery aging is driven by complex interactions among cycling behavior, operating conditions, and cell chemistry, making accurate probabilistic state-of-health (SOH) trajectory modeling across heterogeneous chemistries underexplored.
insight.approach: The authors introduce FlowBatt, which uses flow matching with a diffusion transformer (DiT) backbone to model full SOH trajectories as probabilistic processes conditioned on early-cycle capacity data. They also use explainable AI to diagnose and improve the encoder mapping early-cycle capacity matrices to conditioning vectors.
key_findings: FlowBatt achieves the best trajectory-wise SOH prediction performance on all five public benchmark datasets, with errors below 2.5%.
It delivers competitive remaining useful life (RUL) prediction performance compared to established baselines.
By generating multiple plausible trajectories, FlowBatt provides empirical prediction intervals for battery degradation modeling.
Synthesis experiments show that FlowBatt-generated SOH trajectories reduce random-forest RMSE and MAPE on MATR-1 by approximately 26% and 19%, respectively.
insight.limitations: Prediction remains challenging on MATR-2 and HUST (reflected in higher RUL errors and more pronounced undercoverage of prediction intervals). The model conditions only on fixed 20- or 100-cycle capacity windows without direct temperature, current-profile, charging-protocol, environmental, or cooling inputs, and does not explicitly enforce physical or electrochemical constraints.
insight.why_it_matters: It provides a unified, trajectory-level probabilistic framework for battery health prediction, uncertainty estimation, and aging synthesis that generalizes across diverse chemistries and helps improve downstream remaining useful life (RUL) forecasting.

papers.title: Frequency-Calibrated Decision-Focused Learning for BESS Dispatch Under Renewable Uncertainty
papers.abstract: Battery energy storage system (BESS) flexibility depends on state of charge and intertemporal operating constraints. Renewable forecast errors of similar magnitudes can lead to different BESS dispatch results. An error may alter early charging or discharging decisions and reduce the flexibility available for subsequent regulation, while another may have little effect on the resulting schedule. To account for these unequal consequences, this paper proposes Frequency-Calibrated Decision-Focused Learning (FC-DFL), which trains renewable predictors using the realized operating costs of their induced BESS schedules. Gaussian smoothing and solver-based zeroth-order estimation provide training feedback without requiring differentiating through the non-differentiable mixed-integer BESS dispatch problem. The same decision feedback is further combined with prediction sensitivity to develop a decision-oriented XAI method that identifies the input features and forecast periods most consequential to BESS operation. Case studies using German wind and solar data show that FC-DFL reduces the integrated absolute frequency-deviation metric by 6.05% and decision regret by 23.92% relative to accuracy-based predict-then-optimize method. The XAI analysis further demonstrates that the identified high-impact forecast periods produce 2.84 times larger average absolute changes in realized operating cost than low-impact periods. These findings highlight the importance of incorporating downstream decision-making outcomes into renewable forecasting and demonstrate the value of FC-DFL in improving BESS regulation and providing operationally meaningful forecast explanations.

insight.tldr: The paper introduces Frequency-Calibrated Decision-Focused Learning (FC-DFL) to train renewable energy predictors based on the downstream operational outcomes of BESS dispatch, rather than relying solely on traditional statistical error metrics.
insight.problem: Traditional renewable forecasting methods are trained using statistical accuracy metrics like mean squared error, which fail to capture how forecast errors actually impact downstream BESS dispatch decisions, state-of-charge constraints, and operating costs.
insight.approach: The authors propose FC-DFL, which uses Gaussian smoothing and solver-based zeroth-order estimation to provide training feedback from realized operating costs without needing to differentiate through the non-differentiable mixed-integer BESS dispatch problem. They also combine this feedback with prediction sensitivity to create a decision-oriented explainable AI (XAI) method.
key_findings: FC-DFL reduces the integrated absolute frequency-deviation metric by 6.05% relative to the accuracy-based predict-then-optimize method.
Decision regret is reduced by 23.92% compared to traditional accuracy-based approaches.
BESS energy throughput was reduced by 61.17%.
High-impact forecast periods identified by the XAI analysis produce 2.84 times larger average absolute changes in realized operating cost compared to low-impact periods.
insight.limitations: Future work will extend FC-DFL to network-constrained BESS operation and dynamic frequency-response models.
insight.why_it_matters: For battery management systems, state-of-charge (SOC) availability and intertemporal operating constraints dictate how a battery responds to renewable uncertainty. By aligning forecasting directly with BESS dispatch and operational outcomes, the method improves frequency regulation and offers insights into which forecast periods and input features are most consequential to system operation and battery utilization.

papers.title: Cross-Domain Joint-Embedding Pretraining For Heterogeneous Industrial Time Series
papers.abstract: Industrial predictive maintenance and manufacturing tasks frequently contain abundant sensor measurements, but with limited labeled data. We investigate cross-domain self-supervised pretraining using joint-embedding predictive architecture for heterogeneous industrial time series (JEPA-HITS), which learns one encoder from various domains such as battery, semiconductor chemical mechanical planarization (CMP), computer numerical control (CNC) machining, and bearing while preserving dataset-specific temporal scales. We evaluate representation reuse on regression and classification problems under reduced-label downstream training, and leave-one-domain-out (LODO) pretraining. Compared with the same architecture initialized randomly, LODO pretraining reduces RMSE from 10.72 to 7.95 on battery remaining useful life (RUL), 4.34 to 3.89 on CMP, and 13.53 to 11.72 on tool wear regression, while improving bearing fault diagnosis macro-F1 from 0.547 to 0.737. Overall results suggest that unlabeled time series measurements from heterogeneous industrial processes can provide reusable representations for downstream learning with limited labeled data.

insight.tldr: The paper introduces JEPA-HITS, a cross-domain self-supervised pretraining approach using a joint-embedding predictive architecture to learn a shared encoder across heterogeneous industrial time series. It demonstrates that unlabeled data from varied physical domains can improve downstream tasks like remaining useful life regression even when labels are scarce.
insight.problem: Industrial predictive maintenance and manufacturing tasks frequently contain abundant sensor measurements, but labeled data for degradation and faults are scarce and expensive. Transfer learning across physically distinct industrial domains remains underexplored because existing models often assume fixed input lengths, specific modalities, or focus only on related datasets.
insight.approach: The authors propose Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture for Heterogeneous Industrial Time Series (JEPA-HITS). This method learns a single channel-independent latent encoder across various domains—such as battery, semiconductor CMP, CNC machining, and bearing—while preserving dataset-specific temporal scales via multi-domain loss aggregation. They evaluate representation reuse under reduced-label downstream training and leave-one-domain-out (LODO) pretraining.
key_findings: Leave-one-domain-out (LODO) pretraining reduces RMSE from 10.72 to 7.95 on battery remaining useful life (RUL) regression compared to a randomly initialized architecture.
LODO pretraining reduces RMSE from 4.34 to 3.89 on CMP and from 13.53 to 11.72 on tool wear regression.
LODO pretraining improves bearing fault diagnosis macro-F1 from 0.547 to 0.737.
Unlabeled time series measurements from heterogeneous industrial processes provide reusable representations for downstream learning with limited labeled data.
insight.limitations: The work is not evaluated on extreme cases with signal outliers, missing data, and distribution shifts.
insight.why_it_matters: For battery management systems, this method allows models to leverage abundant sensor data from diverse industrial processes to improve remaining useful life (RUL) prediction and degradation modelling, even when labeled battery degradation data are scarce.

papers.title: Distilling Large-Scale Machine Learning Interatomic Potentials to Predict Long-Timescale Electrolyte Transport Properties
papers.abstract: Accurately predicting the transport properties of liquid electrolytes is critical for next-generation battery design and requires force fields that are both quantum-mechanically accurate and fast enough for long-timescale simulation. Recent large-scale pretrained machine learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) approach density-functional-theory accuracy, but remain too slow to access the necessary timescales to converge transport properties. We provide a knowledge distillation procedure to transfer the accuracy of a large-scale "teacher" MLIP into fast, system-specific "students", without any additional ab initio data. Our distilled models run ~40x faster, reproduce teacher-predicted structural observables, and produce stable 20 ns trajectories in days, rather than the months the teacher would require. Across a diverse set of sodium- and lithium-ion electrolytes, student-predicted self-diffusivities, ionic conductivities, and shear viscosities track experiment and outperform classical force-field predictions, establishing distillation as a practical route to accurate, long-timescale simulations necessary for high-throughput electrolyte screening.
